findings.message: The fd-duplication alternative `\d*>&\d+-?` has no boundary after the digits. Bash reads `>&2out` as a redirect of stdout and stderr to a file named `2out`, but the regex strips only `>&2` and leaves `out` as a plain word. No `<` or `>` remains, so the call passes the new `[<>]` check, which is the guard added to stop file writes. Add a lookahead `(?=[\s;&|]|$)` after the fd alternative, as the /dev/null branch already has, so `>&2x` and `2>&1x` keep their `>` and are denied. Add deny rows for `>&2x`, `2>&1x` and `>&file`.
findings.scenario: In block mode, `git log >&2out` becomes `git log  out` after the strip. It matches ALLOWED and contains no `<` or `>`, so it passes with exit 0 and writes a file named `2out`. The documented rule is that a call can never write a file.
